paper_metadata.title: Simultaneously enhancing strength and plasticity in AlMoNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloys via powder metallurgy

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: This study presented a powder metallurgy (PM) strategy combining mechanical alloying (MA) and spark plasma sintering (SPS) for fabricating the high-performance AlMoNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs), which are composed of BCC phases, ordered B2 phases and grain boundary Al4 Zr5 intermetallics.

evidence.section: 2.1 Materials preparation
evidence.quote: the mechanically alloyed AlMo0.5 NbTa0.5 TiZr powders were successfully achieved. The average size of mechanically alloyed AlMo0.5 NbTa0.5 TiZr powders was conﬁrmed to be reduced to 9.96 μm

evidence.section: 3.1 Fabrication of mechanically alloyed AlMo0.5 NbTa0.5 TiZr powders
evidence.quote: Until the ball milling time was extended to 50 h, all the respective characteristic diffraction peaks of elemental Al, Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti and Zr disappeared completely, instead, only two phases with BCC structure could be detected out

evidence.section: 2.1 Materials preparation
evidence.quote: the high-performance AlMo0.5 NbTa0.5 TiZr and Al0.5 Mo0.5 NbTa0.5 TiZr0.5 RHEAs with the corresponding theoretical densities of 7.4 g/cm3 and 7.85 g/cm3 by powder metallurgy

evidence.section: 3.2.1 Effect of sintering temperature on final microstructures
evidence.quote: the microstructure of as-SPSed AlMo0.5 NbTa0.5 TiZr RHEA sintered at 1400 °C consisted of light gray intragranular phases, dark gray grain boundary phases with a continuous striplike morphology

parameters.cooling_method: interrupted every 50 min for 10 min cooling

evidence.section: 2.1 Materials preparation
evidence.quote: The mechanical alloying of these different metal element powders was conducted in a planetary ball mill (QM-3SP4, Nanjing NanDa Instrument Plant) with a ball-to-powder weight ratio of 12:1 at a speed of 360 rpm under an argon atmosphere.

evidence.section: 2.1 Materials preparation
evidence.quote: the mechanically alloyed AlMoNbTaTiZr powders were consolidated via SPS in a graphite mold with a 40 mm inner diameter. The SPS process was carried out at temperatures ranging from 1400 °C to 1600 °C for 20 min, with an axial pressure of 50 MPa applied in vacuum ( < 1.3 × 10−2 Pa).

evidence.section: 3.5 Influence of Al/Zr content on microstructure and mechanical properties
evidence.quote: the Al0.5 Mo0.5 NbTa0.5 TiZr0.5 RHEA with the lower content of Al and Zr was produced by spark plasma sintering at 1500 °C. The alloyed Al0.5 Mo0.5 NbTa0.5 TiZr0.5 powders were prepared using the same ball milling process and parameters as those used for AlMo0.5 NbTa0.5 TiZr.

evidence.quote: only two phases with BCC structure could be detected out and the corresponding lattice parameters were calculated to be 3.40 0 0 ˚A and 3.0617 ˚A

evidence.section: 3.2.1 Effect of sintering temperature on final microstructures
evidence.quote: the dark gray grain boundary phases were enriched in Al and Zr elements, in conjunction with SAED analysis in Fig. 4 (c), which could be identiﬁed as Al4 Zr5 intermetallics with a typical hexagonal crystal structure.

evidence.section: 3.2.1 Effect of sintering temperature on final microstructures
evidence.quote: the intragranular phases were composed of disordered BCC phases and ordered B2 phases, and their orientation relationship was < 100 >BCC // < 100 >B2 and {001}BCC //{001}B2

evidence.section: 3.2.1 Effect of sintering temperature on final microstructures
evidence.quote: the SAED patterns revealed that the intragranular phases were composed of disordered BCC phases and ordered B2 phases

evidence.section: 3.2.1 Effect of sintering temperature on final microstructures
evidence.quote: simultaneous Zr and O enrichments were found in the dot-like particles, which were conﬁrmed as ZrO2 phases with the monoclinic crystal structure

evidence.section: 3.2.1 Effect of sintering temperature on final microstructures
evidence.quote: the grain boundary phases were enriched in Al (32 at. %) and Zr (41 at. %) ... they could be identiﬁed as Al4 Zr5 intermetallics. Instead of continuous striplike morphologies obtained by sintering at 1400 °C, the Al4 Zr5 intermetallics achieved by sintering at 1500 °C exhibited a desired discontinuous distribution at the grain boundary.

evidence.section: 3.2.2 Constituent phases evolution at different sintering temperatures
evidence.quote: the content of the ordered B2 phases ﬁrst rose from 21.95 % at 1400 °C to 32.33 % at 1500 °C, and then declined to 12.61 % at 1600 °C.

evidence.section: 3.2.2 Constituent phases evolution at different sintering temperatures
evidence.quote: As the sintering temperature increased from 1400 °C to 1500 °C, both the average edge width of BCC phases and the average channel width of B2 phases increased

evidence.section: 3.2.2 Constituent phases evolution at different sintering temperatures
evidence.quote: the content of Al4 Zr5 intermetallics gradually increased, from 5.3 % at 1400 °C to 12.3 % at 1500 °C, and ﬁnally to 35.8 % at 1600 °C. Moreover, the Al4 Zr5 intermetallics exhibited signiﬁcant morphological changes from a continuous striplike distribution along grain boundaries at 1400 °C, to a discontinuous grain boundary distribution at 1500 °C, and ﬁnally to a randomly equiaxed morphology at 1600 °C.

evidence.section: 3.2.2 Constituent phases evolution at different sintering temperatures
evidence.quote: nanosized B2 phases with a low degree of ordering precipitated within disordered BCC phases, instead of a BCC/B2 coherent structure.

evidence.section: 3.2.2 Constituent phases evolution at different sintering temperatures
evidence.quote: the microstructure of the AlMo0.5 NbTa0.5 TiZr RHEA sintered at 1600 °C contained equiaxed BCC phases with nanosized ordered B2 phases

attributes.size: microsized particles ~1 μm, nanosized striplike phases ~160 nm width

evidence.section: 3.5 Influence of Al/Zr content on microstructure and mechanical properties
evidence.quote: the microstructure of the Al0.5 Mo0.5 NbTa0.5 TiZr0.5 RHEA consisted of light gray grains with an area percentage of 95.3 %, dark gray grain boundary phases with an area percentage of 4.2 %, and a small quantity of dark gray dot-like particles, corresponding to BCC/B2 phases, grain boundary Al4 Zr5 intermetallics and ZrO2 phases

evidence.section: 3.5 Influence of Al/Zr content on microstructure and mechanical properties

evidence.section: 3.5 Influence of Al/Zr content on microstructure and mechanical properties
